newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - March 13.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- PHONE USE GROWS AS MORE PREFER SURFING TO TALKING

An analysis from the Financial Times has revealed the use of the Internet and other on-line services linked to PCs now accounts for about 10 percent of local telephone call traffic, and for much of its growth. The research shows inland call volume in the UK grew 7 percent during 1996, buoyed by a rise in Internet use that is estimated at 10 percent to 15 percent a month. However, some telecoms companies have warned the growth of the Internet threatens to overload the world's telecoms networks.
-- TORIES PLAN MORE UNION CURBS DESPITE CRITICISM

The general election manifesto of the Conservative party is likely to include a pledge for controversial new legislation curbing trade union power. The proposals, which would allow the public to sue unions in monopoly public services if strikes cause 'disproportionate cost', have already been criticised by the CBI and other groups. Trade secretary Ian Lang has confirmed that a consultation exercise with companies and organizations has been completed, though it is reported the responses are predominantly negative.
-- BARROW YEAR BEATS GOVAN TO NAVY OIL TANKER DEAL

The Kvaerner Govan shipyard on the Clyde has been left facing heavy redundancies and possible closure within a year after losing out on a 200m stg order for two Royal Navy oil tankers. The contract, which the MoD said had been awarded on value for money grounds, has gone to VSEL, the Barrow shipyard owned by GEC. However, Ian Davidson, the Labour MP for Govan, has said he will be asking the National Audit Office and the Commons Public Accounts Committee to investigate the award of the contract after accusing VSEL of unfair competition.
-- BIOTECH COMPANIES SHOW STRONG GROWTH

A report due to be published Thursday by accountants and management consultants Arthur Andersen will underline the growth of the UK's biotechnology sector. The report shows the number of companies in the industry has more than doubled in the past two years, as has employment in the sector. However, the report cautions that continued growth in the sector depends on finding at least 1 billion stg of funding in the next two years.
-- SBC WARBURG RULES OUT US PURCHASE

Investment bank SBC Warburg has announced a 54 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profits, from SFr663 million to SFr1.025 billion (439 million stg). Announcing the results, SBC Warburg chairman Hans de Gier ruled out an immediate acquisition to bolster its operations in the United States, suggesting he may wait for US commercial banks to start buying investment banks on Wall Street and then benefit from the upheaval by hiring teams of traders that 'came loose'.
-- RENTOKIL SHARES FALL 9 PERCENT AS CORE GROWTH SLOWS

Shares in services group Rentokil Initial fell 9 percent on Wednesday after the company announced slower growth in its core cleaning and pest control businesses. Rentokil, which became the world's biggest services group last spring after acquiring BET for 2.3 billion stg, reported a 48 percent increase in pre-tax profits in the year to December 31, to 318 million stg. However, underlying profits growth at the original Rentokil businesses slowed to just 6.25 percent.
-- BP OIL AND GAS OUTPUT TO SURGE

British Petroleum has said oil and gas output will jump by two-thirds during the next decade to 2.5 million barrels a day, with the growth in output being matched by annual additions of new reserves. In a presentation to investment analysts Wednesday, BP confirmed it and its partners had made two big discoveries last year, one off Australia and one off Angola.
-- TELEWEST BECOMES EARNINGS POSITIVE FOR FIRST TIME

Cable company Telewest has become earnings positive for the first time after reporting that annual pre-tax losses more than doubled at 249.9 million stg. Telewest, the UK's second biggest cable company, announced earnings of 465,000 stg before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation, compared with losses of 28 million stg last year. The company is planning to launch a digital service later this year offering video-on-demand, home shopping and fast Internet access.
-- CORTECS SPENDS 4.6 MILLION STG ON R&D

Biotechnology company Cortecs International has reported a near-tripling of losses in the six months to December 31, to 4.3 million stg. Research and development costs rose 84 percent during the period, to 4.6 million stg, as the company put its lead product, Macritonin, through the final stages of clinical trials. Cortecs plans to seek authorisation to market Macritonin, a treatment for osteoporosis, in Europe if initial results from trials are positive.
-- JAPANESE TELECOMS GROUPS TO MERGE

Japan is see its first-ever merger in its telecoms industry with the alliance this autumn of long-distance operator Japan Telecom and the international carrier International Telecom Japan. The merger will create Japan's second-largest telecoms company in terms of revenues, after Nippon Telegraph and Telephone. The move follows the decision last year by the government to remove barriers between domestic and international telecoms, and to allow a demerged NTT into the international market within the next two years.
